prompt: Hold a group of threads at a start gate, release them all at once, and wait for every one to report in -- using two CountDownLatches. Complete runTogether, then run the tests.
explanation: A CountDownLatch is a one-shot gate: await() blocks until the count reaches zero, and countDown() can never push it back up. A latch of 1 makes a start gate that releases every waiting worker at the same instant, while a latch of workerCount makes a finish line the main thread can await instead of joining each Thread by hand. The countDown must live in a finally block, because a worker that dies from an exception without counting down would leave await() blocked forever -- the classic way a latch-based program hangs.
hints: You need two latches: new CountDownLatch(1) for the gate and new CountDownLatch(workerCount) for the finish line.
Inside each worker: startGate.await(), then job.run(), then count a success; wrap the whole thing so doneLatch.countDown() sits in a finally.
Count successes with an AtomicInteger -- several workers increment it at once, and only the main thread reads it after doneLatch.await() returns.
